definition: searching widely for food or provisions
memoryTip: For-aging: searching for food (or material) out in the wild.
correctPassage: The documentary follows bears foraging for salmon along the river.
wrongPassages: Leadership tried to foraging NPS by surveying only known promoters.
The tramp dock looked foraging with no lines on any bollard.
He offered a foraging compromise neither side’s written demands could accept.

definition: in a way not directly expressed; absolutely
memoryTip: Im-plied, not said out loud — understood between the lines.
correctPassage: By remaining silent, the board implicitly endorsed the chair’s decision.
wrongPassages: He searched implicitly by opening the first result and never scrolling further.
She argued implicitly by repeating the claim louder each time it was challenged.
He spoke implicitly so that every word was swallowed and nobody took notes.

memoryTip: A-finity: natural “fit” / liking for something.
correctPassage: She felt an immediate affinity for the spare, geometric style of the paintings.
wrongPassages: She stored the affinity next to batteries and tape in the utility closet.
He dropped a pin named affinity on a mall parking space.
The bin tagged affinity held cables cut at both ends.

definition: division into parts; a dividing wall
memoryTip: Part + ition — divides into parts (or a dividing wall).
correctPassage: A temporary partition divided the gallery into two smaller exhibition rooms.
wrongPassages: Tuesday navigation to pin partition was a habit without a purpose.
He finally matched one lock using a key from the old partition drawer.
Folder partition was deleted after thumbs.db was gone.

memoryTip: A-dept (depth of skill) — really good at it.
correctPassage: She is adept at turning dense research into clear public explanations.
wrongPassages: The marina looked adept in winter with every slip empty.
The call center hoped to adept transfers by removing the transfer key entirely.
The desk hoped to adept transfers by removing agent-to-agent routing.

definition: optimistic, especially in a difficult situation
memoryTip: From blood/sang — rosy-cheeked optimist even when things look bad.
correctPassage: Despite the delays, the director remained sanguine about the opening date.
wrongPassages: The reprise felt sanguine because key and tempo had both shifted.
The submediant held was sanguine under an ending that sat only on I.
The coda’s sanguine idea belonged in a different piece entirely.

memoryTip: Only a notion — theoretical, not yet real.
correctPassage: The budget included only a notional amount for travel until actual costs were known.
wrongPassages: He set severity to notional after legal review had already escalated it.
The station’s notional gate display counted down to a train that never came.
The sérac traverse felt notional on a marked winter route with wands.

memoryTip: Slumber = sleep — makes you drowsy.
correctPassage: The heat and the soft music had a slumberous effect on the audience.
wrongPassages: Fans called the deluxe remaster slumberous for loudness that crushed dynamics.
The subtonic drone was slumberous under a Picardy third that ignored it.
He treated the formality as slumberous and skipped it without consequence.

definition: having the ability to restore health or strength
memoryTip: Restores you — rest that heals energy.
correctPassage: A weekend by the lake proved restorative after months of deadline pressure.
wrongPassages: The plaza design was restorative: benches faced away from one another.
The terminal’s restorative art wall was a vinyl wrap of a different airport.
She closed the PIR as restorative before any interviews were scheduled.

definition: make information known; give a quality
memoryTip: Im-part: give a part of knowledge or a quality to someone.
correctPassage: Good mentors impart not only techniques but also habits of careful reading.
wrongPassages: He tried to impart the contempt order by posting the sealed filing online.
The monitor will impart escalations by looping them into an unread channel.
She hoped to impart the walkout by docking the planning lunch as unpaid time.

memoryTip: No warrant (no justification) — not called for.
correctPassage: The criticism was unwarranted; the study had carefully controlled for bias.
wrongPassages: an unwarranted border crossing still requires passports, checks, and stamps.
The bog hollow stayed unwarranted after every free-running ditch lowered it.
His unwarranted limitation clause ran longer than the rest of the agreement.

memoryTip: Ex-orbit: way outside the orbit of a fair price — too high.
correctPassage: Residents complained about the exorbitant fees charged by the utility company.
wrongPassages: Her exorbitant testimony contradicted itself on both times and names.
Her exorbitant printer note described a binding style never used in production.
Fans called the live-stream mix exorbitant for chat audio over the performance.

memoryTip: De-mark a boundary line — set the borders.
correctPassage: A stone wall was built to demarcate the boundary between the two farms.
wrongPassages: She hoped to demarcate the mutiny optics by purging the chat history overnight.
The cron will demarcate SLA breaches by changing the SLA definition mid-month.
The bot will demarcate the ticket by closing it with “thanks!” and no solution.

memoryTip: You can “get” the intelligence of it — understandable.
correctPassage: Even without technical training, the diagram makes the process intelligible.
wrongPassages: Voters defeated the intelligible levy that schools said would prevent cuts.
The epilogue was intelligible: it opened a sequel instead of closing the story.
The floodplain stayed intelligible behind a levee raised after the last crest.

memoryTip: Use your discreet judgment — careful choice / privacy.
correctPassage: Hiring decisions are left to the manager’s discretion within stated guidelines.
wrongPassages: The permit titled discretion had a gold seal and no operative language.
The crate stamped discretion held bubble wrap and nothing else of value.
The routing code discretion bounced every message to the mailroom floor.

memoryTip: Not pretentious — simple, no showing off.
correctPassage: The café’s unpretentiousness—plain tables, no music—was part of its appeal.
wrongPassages: She wrote unpretentiousness as a bullet and never returned to fill it in.
The sticker book’s unpretentiousness was a gold star for “participation.”
The cookbook treated unpretentiousness as a cute name for “a splash.”

memoryTip: Sub + side: sink down / calm down (flood, anger).
correctPassage: Once the fever began to subside, she was able to sleep through the night.
wrongPassages: The snow cornice felt subside behind a seasonal fence and signs.
Historians labeled the decade subside once complete archives left almost nothing in doubt.
Trustees cut the subside arts grant that local schools had already matched.

memoryTip: A practical joke — playful trick.
correctPassage: What started as a harmless prank escalated into a costly misunderstanding.
wrongPassages: The team hoped to prank reopen rates by locking closed tickets permanently.
The bog hollow stayed prank after drains lowered the entire water table.
Viewers found the remake prank for matching the original runtime to the second.

definition: reveal the presence of a quality or feeling
memoryTip: E-vince: evidence shows; it “evinces” a quality.
correctPassage: The early drafts already evince the precision that would mark her mature style.
wrongPassages: She practiced the speech evince until every pause landed the same way.
The alliance was evince: both sides published the full text of every clause.
The decree was evince until translators agreed on one English text.

memoryTip: Pre-clude: close the door in advance — make it impossible.
correctPassage: A prior commitment precludes her from joining the evening session.
wrongPassages: They tried to preclude the sinkhole by filling it with uncompacted trash.
He moved to preclude the deposition by claiming he “doesn’t recall” every fact.
She tried to preclude the relapse by returning immediately to the same triggers.
